title: FedEMA-Distill: Exponential Moving Average Guided Knowledge Distillation for Robust Federated Learning

C-a.quote: it retains the logits-only uplink and heterogeneity support of distillation-based FL, while injecting temporal smoothing through server-side EMA and improving robustness via robust logit aggregation.
C-a.locator: §2 Positioning and quantitative comparison; THIS IS THE PAPER'S OWN DISTRIBUTION OF ROLES and it assigns robustness to the aggregation rule, not to the EMA. Only ONE component carries a stated purpose of resisting corrupted updates: the robust logit aggregator, "For improved robustness, the server can use a coordinatewise median or trimmed mean instead, which downweights outlier values (defending against any corrupted or anomalous client logits)." (§3), reinforced at "These robust aggregation rules are commonly used to mitigate Byzantine clients in FL (Yin et al., 2018) and can be applied at the logit level as well" (§3) and in the contributions list, "(3) Robustness to adversarial clients at the logit level: coordinate-wise median/trimmed-mean secure training with up to ∼20% Byzantine clients" (§1). EXCLUDED UNDER AMENDMENT 3, each with its own purpose quotation: the EMA stage, whose stated job is temporal smoothing of the global iterate, "and then applies an Exponential Moving Average (EMA) to the global model weights before the next round." (§1), and whose ablation-section purpose is stability, "The ablations support the stability role of EMA-guided distillation. Removing EMA (𝛽 = 0) increases round-to-round fluctuations and leads to noisier convergence" (§5.6); the logits-only uplink, whose purpose is communication cost; the knowledge-distillation stage, "A complementary thread performs output-level aggregation via knowledge distillation (KD), which can cut uplink and naturally support heterogeneous client models." (§2); and the anchor term, "Anchor 𝜇: small 𝜇 (e.g., 10−4 ) stabilizes without slowing; too large slows learning" (§5.6), which is the numerical-stability kind of purpose clause -- the second instance in the frame after SecureDyn-FL's parameter clipping. TWO JOINT COUNTER-QUOTATIONS EXIST AND ARE THE READING THIS CODE DECLINES: the abstract's "These results indicate that coupling temporal smoothing with logits-only aggregation provides a communication-efficient and attack-resilient FL pipeline" and Table 1's caption, "FedEMA-Distill combines the strengths of weight-averaging and logits distillation: small client uploads and heterogeneity support (like FedDF), plus improved stability and robustness (via EMA and robust aggregation).".

C-b.quote: driftreduction methods provide temporal stability but don’t reduce communication, while output-distillation methods save communication but can introduce instability in non-IID settings. There is a gap in jointly addressing both facets.
C-b.locator: §2; this is the paper's only reciprocal-deficiency argument and BOTH of the constituents it pairs are excluded from C-a under Amendment 3 -- drift reduction (the EMA) and output distillation (the logits-only KD), traded off on temporal stability against communication cost. The same argument in its positioning form is "Distillation-only pipelines achieve strong communication efficiency and model-architecture heterogeneity but may exhibit higher round-to-round variance under strong label skew. Momentum EMA-only server updates stabilize optimization but still require weight uploads. FedEMA-Distill explicitly couples logits-only aggregation with EMA smoothing of the global weights to deliver temporal continuity, reduced uplink, and robustness using simple robust statistics on logits, without any client-side code changes." (§2). No reason of any kind is given for pairing the ONE counted defense component with anything; the robust statistic enters as an option, "The server aggregates these logits (optionally using robust statistics), performs a brief knowledge distillation (KD) step to update the global model" (§1), and the composed claim states what the coupling delivers rather than why the constituents were chosen for each other.

This is the FedSAC random-clustering shape and cleaner: a single upstream rule varies, one arm of it is the no-defense case, and nothing downstream moves. THE §5.6 ABLATIONS ARE NOT THE EVIDENCE AND ARE DECLINED FOR TWO DIFFERENT REASONS: "5.6. Ablations EMA factor 𝛽: 𝛽=0 (no EMA) is noisier and slightly lower final accuracy; 𝛽=0.9 best; 𝛽=0.99 too sluggish (Figure 7). Temperature 𝑇 : 𝑇 =1 underperforms; 𝑇 =3–5 best; 𝑇 =8 over-smooths (Figure 8)." -- the beta arm varies the DOWNSTREAM stage, which is the direction the rubric declines, and the T arm varies an upstream knob at four settings but reports no adversarial outcome at all ("Similarly, moderate distillation temperatures(𝑇 = 3–5) provide stable soft targets, while very low 𝑇 behaves closer to hard labels and very high 𝑇 over-smooths, both of which can degrade the quality and stability of the teacher signal.", §5.6), so the attack is ABSENT rather than held fixed and the contrast cannot identify any defense's dependence on its input.

coder_note:
THE DISTRIBUTIVE TEST, ARTICULATED AT ROW 47 AND NOT FROZEN IN ADVANCE, DECIDES C-a HERE. The paper makes two JOINT attributions -- the abstract's "coupling temporal smoothing with logits-only aggregation provides a communication-efficient and attack-resilient FL pipeline" and Table 1's "improved stability and robustness (via EMA and robust aggregation)" -- either of which, read as distributing over both constituents, would give the EMA stage a stated defense purpose and take C-a to YES on two components. Under FedSAC (2503.18284) I coded C-a = YES on exactly that grammar. The difference, and it is decisive, is that THIS paper elsewhere distributes the roles itself: "injecting temporal smoothing through server-side EMA and improving robustness via robust logit aggregation" assigns stability to the EMA and robustness to the aggregator, one clause each. FedSAC has no such sentence. So the rule is: when a paper attributes a conjunction of benefits to a conjunction of components, look for a sentence where it distributes them; if one exists, the distribution governs and the joint sentence is not a purpose statement for either component alone. Rule 3 points the same way, so this is not a rule-3 call -- it is the paper's own division of labour. A5 must report the distributive test alongside the granularity rule (row 45) as the second adjudication rule that Amendment 3's text does not settle, and must note that both were articulated mid-coding and are disclosed rather than retrofitted.

C-a = NO COSTS THE FRAME NOTHING AND THE PRIMARY IS NO UNDER EVERY READING. C-d = YES on Table 7 independently, so even a reader who takes the abstract's joint clause as EMA's purpose, codes C-a = YES and then also reaches C-b = YES lands at DESIGN = YES and primary = NO. Nothing in the totals moves on the distributive test except the DESIGN denominator's membership, and this row joins SRFed as the second row with C-a = NO and C-d = YES.

C-b IS THE FOURTH INSTANCE OF AMENDMENT 3'S EXCISED-CONSTITUENT LIMIT, AND IT CORRECTS THE GENERALIZATION THE THIRD INSTANCE DREW. The prior three are 2601.04930 (PPFA-BA: the residual-coverage reason refers to the inclusion mechanism, excised as fairness/debiasing), 2601.06466 (SecureDyn-FL: the Complementary Protection bullet pairs temporal gradient auditing with ENCRYPTION), and 2602.22269 (CQSA: the blinding-tension sentence pairs SECURE AGGREGATION with Byzantine detection). CQSA's note concluded that "the excised constituent is always the PRIVACY one"; that was already inexact -- PPFA-BA's was a fairness mechanism -- and this row settles it, because here BOTH excised constituents are non-privacy, one communication-purposed and one heterogeneity-purposed. A5 must carry the corrected version: the limit is not privacy-specific, and two of the four instances involve no privacy mechanism at all. Here the pairing reason is a clean reciprocal-deficiency argument of the admissible COST-COMPLEMENTARITY kind -- drift reduction gives temporal stability but not communication savings, output distillation gives savings but round-to-round instability -- and BOTH of its constituents are excised, one for a communication purpose and one for a heterogeneity purpose. That the pattern reproduces with two entirely different non-defense purposes is the strongest evidence yet for the A5 recommendation that the purpose test be applied PER PAIR rather than per component: the deficiency chain is exactly the reasoning C-b was written to detect, and the criterion cannot see it because the pair is not a defense pair. Stated the other way, this paper composes for a reason and its reason is not about poisoning at all.

AND THE PAPER'S CLAIMED DEFENSE PAIRING IS NOT THE PAIRING ITS OWN RESULT IDENTIFIES. The abstract credits attack-resilience to "temporal smoothing with logits-only aggregation"; the only adversarial measurement in the paper, Table 7, varies neither of those -- it varies the aggregation RULE, and the entire effect it reports (50.0 percent at the mean, 78.0 percent at the median) is attributable to the robust statistic, which that clause does not name. So the composed system's advertised robustness pairing and its measured robustness contrast are about different components. This is a new exhibit for A3 and a mild one: not an unmeasured interaction claim like PQ-BRFL's or SecureDyn-FL's, but a MISALIGNED one, where a real contrast was run on a component other than the one the claim names.

A NEW DECLINED-ROUTE REASON, NOT SEEN BEFORE IN THE FRAME: THE ATTACK-ABSENT CONTRAST. The temperature sweep in §5.6 has the right SHAPE for C-d -- T is a client-side, upstream knob, results are reported at four settings (T = 1, 3, 5, 8), and the downstream KD and EMA stages are fixed -- and it clears the hyperparameter route's reported-results floor that the SpectralKrum row established. It still fails, because the sweep runs in the clean setting: C-d requires the attack HELD FIXED, and an experiment with no adversaries does not hold the attack fixed at anything, it removes the object the contrast is supposed to be about. A5 should record this next to the hyperparameter floor, because the two together state what that route requires: more than one setting reported, and an adversarial outcome at each. Had Table 7 not existed, this row would have been C-d = NO on that ground alone -- and it would then have been a primary only if C-a and C-b had also gone the other way, which the distributive test and the excised-pair finding both forbid.

EXTRACTOR PERFORMANCE, WORST IN THE FRAME ON THE TWO BUCKETS THAT MATTER. C-c returned ZERO candidates over 65744 characters -- the sixteenth zero-candidate C-c bucket, and a FALSE negative, since Table 7 and Figure 3 are both present; the vocabulary that defeated it is the absence of ASR and backdoor, the same failure as BROADCAST, DP-BREM, BRFL and DDFed. C-d returned two candidates, both dataset-setup sentences, and missed Table 7 entirely: the seventeenth C-d shortfall. C-e returned two candidates, one of them a sentence from the AUTHOR BIOGRAPHY at the end of this Elsevier preprint ("He actively contributes to the research community as the founder of the UNet conference..."), which is a new kind of false candidate -- back-matter prose scored as evidence -- and worth one line in A5's aid-performance paragraph, because a coder skimming candidate lists could quote it. Every coded quotation on this row came from targeted greps and from reading §3, §5.4 and §5.6.

DATA-QUALITY NOTE, RECORDED AND NOT ACTED ON. There are no theorem, lemma or proposition environments (0 hits each), 3 seeds with reported standard deviations, and the robustness section is a single paragraph with one table. The attacks are label-flip and random-logit, both untargeted at the logit level, so this row contributes nothing to the frame's backdoor-specific counts. It stays in the frame under non-negotiable 7.
